Choose fields...	
Choose which fields are shown, also the technical ones

Choose metadata fields	
Checked fields are shown on the Metadata tab. Normally only the common fields are shown, the others are mostly technical values.	
Show all fields of every file	
Field	
Value	
Name in Windows	
Only common fields	
%d technical fields are hidden.	
Store To EXE Path	
Only set this to true if writing to the EXE directory makes sense, e.g. on an installation on an USB memory stick. Never set it to true when the EXE is located in the 'Program Files' folder, with Windows versions newer than Windows XP this would not work!	
Single Instance	
If set to true, only one single instance of Lucid Viewer runs at any time, if false multiple instances are allowed Set to true to open all images in the same Lucid Viewer window.	
Skip File Open Dialog On Startup	
Set to true to skip the 'File Open' dialog when starting Lucid Viewer without providing a file name as parameter	
Files Processed By WIC	
File endings of files to be decoded by WIC (Windows Imaging Component) If the Microsoft Camera Codec pack is installed, full size camera RAW files can be read with WIC Add the file endings of the raw files to view here, e.g. FilesProcessedByWIC=*.wdp;*.hdp;*.jxr;*.nef	
File Endings RAW	
File endings of camera RAW files to be searched for embedded JPEG thumb images to display Reading just these embedded JPEGs is much faster than decoding the RAW using WIC	
Display Full Size RAW	
Set behavior for opening RAW files listed in FileEndingsRAW 0: open embedded thumbnail 1: open full size 2: open thumbnail, fallback to full size 3: open full size, fallback to thumbnail	
open embedded thumbnail	
open full size	
open thumbnail, fallback to full size	
open full size, fallback to thumbnail	
Keep Parameters	
Set to true to keep the zoom, pan, contrast, gamma, sharpen and rotation setting between the images	
Display Monitor	
Only for multi-monitor systems! Monitor to start the application on -1: Use monitor with largest resolution, primary monitor if several monitors have the same resolution 0: Use primary monitor 1...n: Use the non-primary monitor with index n	
Use monitor with largest resolution, primary monitor if several monitors have the same resolution	
Use primary monitor	
CPU Type	
CPUType can be AutoDetect, Generic, MMX, SSE or AVX2 Generic should work on all CPUs, MMX needs at least MMX II (starting from PIII) Use AutoDetect to detect the best possible algorithm to use	
CPU Cores Used	
Number of CPU cores used. Set to 0 for auto detection. Must be 1 to 4, or 0 for auto detect.	
Ini Editor	
Editor for INI files notepad : Use notepad.exe system : Use application registered for INI files other : Full path to application for editing INI files, %exepath% placeholder can be used	
Wallpaper Path	
When setting a processed image as desktop wallpaper, the processed image must be saved somewhere. This INI setting sets the path to save the file. Default is %temp%, the system TEMP directory. You must have write access to the specified directory!	
Allow File Deletion	
Set to false to disallow deletion of images in Lucid Viewer. This hides the 'x' button on the navigation panel and disables the commands for deletion (IDM_MOVE_TO_RECYCLE_BIN etc.)	
Language	
Specify language used in the user interface. Set to 'auto' to use the language of the operating system.	
Background Color	
Background color, R G B, each component must be in [0..255], e.g. "128 128 128" for a middle gray	
GUI Color	
GUI colors, R G B format as used by BackgroundColor	
Highlight Color	
Selection Color	
Slider Color	
File Name Color	
Default GUI Font	
GUI font, format: "font name" fontSizeInPoints [bold] 'Default' for the default GUI font of Windows Example: DefaultGUIFont="Arial" 9.0 bold	
Allow Edit Global Settings	
Set to true to show the menu item that allows editing the global INI file option is found under Settings/Admin sub-menu	
Show Full Screen	
Start in full screen or windowed mode 'true' or 'false' to always start in full screen, respectively windowed mode 'auto' to choose best mode depending on image size of first image - windowed when it is small, full screen when it is large	
Single Full Screen Instance	
If set to true, only one single instance of Lucid Viewer runs in full screen mode, if false multiple instances are allowed The value is ignored if SingleInstance=true	
Default Window Rect	
Sets the default position and size of the window in window mode. Possible values: 'auto' for 2/3 of screen size 'max' to start with maximized window 'image' to adjust the window size automatically to the image size 'sticky' to automatically restore the last used window size (when ShowFullScreen=auto only the upper,left position is restored) 'left top right bottom', space separated e.g: 100 100 900 700	
2/3 of screen size	
start with maximized window	
adjust the window size automatically to the image size	
automatically restore the last used window size (when ShowFullScreen=auto only the upper,left position is restored)	
Sticky Window Rect	
Contains the stored window rectangle in case of DefaultWindowRect=sticky	
Minimal Window Size	
Minimal window size in windowed mode (in pixels)	
Window Borderless On Startup	
If set to 'true', window starts in borderless mode (title bar hidden, cannot be manually resized) The window mode can be changed after startup	
Window Always On Top On Startup	
If set to 'true', window starts in always-on-top mode (window will always be visible on top of other windows) The window mode can be changed after startup	
Show Toolbar	
The toolbar (with the main menu), the status bar and the information side panel are shown next to the image, never over it. They are hidden in full screen mode and when the window title bar is hidden. They can also be switched on and off in the View menu, in the context menu and with Ctrl+T (toolbar), Ctrl+I (side panel).	
Show Status Bar	
Show Side Panel	
Side Panel Collapsed	
Side panel collapsed to a narrow strip with icons (toggled with its arrow button)	
Escape Closes Window	
If true, the Esc key closes Lucid Viewer also in window mode (as in older versions). If false, Esc ends the current tool (crop, drawing, compare) and leaves full screen mode.	
Show Start Screen	
Start screen with the last opened photos and the photos pinned by the user, shown when no image is open (Alt+Home). If false, the file open dialog is shown when Lucid Viewer is started without an image.	
Open Last Image	
Started without an image, Lucid Viewer opens the photo viewed last (needs RememberRecentFiles=true)	
Remember Recent Files	
Remember the recently opened photos and show them on the start screen. If false, nothing is written to StartRecent.txt and the recent row stays empty.	
Min Display Size	
Small images are shown zoomed in so that their larger side has at least this size (pixels at 96 DPI) when the zoom mode does not enlarge images. 0 shows them in their original size.	
Smooth Animations	
Smooth zooming with the mouse wheel and the zoom keys, smooth scrolling of the start screen and the thumbnail strip	
Side Panel Width	
Width of the information side panel in pixels (at 96 DPI), 180 to 800	
Chrome Theme	
Colors of toolbar, status bar, side panel and menus: dark or light	
Convert Custom Presets	
Additional conversions for the 'Convert to' menus, separated by semicolons. A conversion is 'format' or 'operation:format' with the formats jpg, png, webp, webpll (lossless), bmp, tiff, gif, ico, pdf and same (format of the source file) and the operations scaleN (N percent), fitN (long edge at most N pixels), rotl, rotr, rot180 and nometa (no EXIF/GPS). Example: ConvertCustomPresets=fit2560:webp;scale30:jpg Run LucidViewer.exe /registerconvertmenu (or Tools menu) again after changing this to update the Explorer menu.	
Convert Output Folder	
Folder for converted files. Empty: next to the source file. A relative name such as 'converted' is a sub folder of the source folder (created when needed), an absolute path is used for all files.	
Screenshot Folder	
Folder of saved screenshots. Empty: Pictures\Screenshots	
Screenshot Hotkey	
Global shortcuts of the screenshot tool in the notification area, e.g. PrintScreen, Shift+PrintScreen, Ctrl+Alt+S, F12. Empty switches a shortcut off. Windows 11 gives the Print Screen key to the Snipping Tool unless this is switched off in Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard.	
Screenshot Text Hotkey	
Screenshot History	
Screenshot history: if true, every screenshot is kept in the screenshot folder (also the ones only copied to the clipboard) and the start screen of the viewer shows them in a row.	
Ocr Language	
Language of the text recognition (OCR), e.g. tr or en-US. The language must be installed in Windows. Empty: the language of a non English keyboard layout, else the Windows display language.	
Show Bottom Panel	
Set to true to show the bottom panel when moving the mouse to the bottom of the screen/window. The bottom panel provides basic image processing functionality	
Show Nav Panel	
Set to false if the navigation panel shall not be blended to the image	
Show Zoom Navigator	
Set to false to disable the thumbnail image blended in during zoom and pan	
Blend Factor Nav Panel	
Blending factor of the navigation panel when the mouse is not on that panel. Set to 0.0 to only show the panel when the mouse is over the panel	
Scale Factor Nav Panel	
Scaling factor for the navigation panel. Increase if the buttons on the panel are too small, e.g. on a touchscreen.	
File Display Order	
Sorting order of the files when displaying the image files in a folder Can be LastModDate, CreationDate, FileName, FileSize, Random, Rating (star rating) or DateTaken (EXIF date the photo was taken)	
File Sort Ascending	
Sort files ascending (increasing, e.g. A->Z, 0->9) or descending (decreasing, e.g. Z->A, 9->0)	
Folder Navigation	
Navigation within or between folders LoopFolder : Loop within the source folder and never leave this folder LoopSameFolderLevel: Loop to next folder on the same hierarchy level (sibling folders) LoopSubFolders: Loop into subfolders of the source folder	
Wrap Around Folder	
If true the files in a folder are shown with wrap around, thus going from last to first image and vice versa If false navigation stops on the last and first image	
Flash Window Alert	
When WrapAroundFolder is false, alert when trying to go to the next file while at the end of the file list, or previous file while at the beginning of file list If true, window flashes briefly when there are no more new images to show If false, there is no visual feedback	
Beep Sound Alert	
When WrapAroundFolder is false, alert when trying to go to the next file while at the end of the file list, or previous file while at the beginning of file list If true, system emits a short beep using the default system sound when there are no more new images to show If false, there is no audio feedback	
Navigate With Mouse Wheel	
If true, the mouse wheel can be used to navigate forward and backward and zoom must be done with Ctrl-MouseWheel If false, zoom is done with the mousewheel (no Ctrl required)	
Exchange X Buttons	
If true, the extended mouse buttons (Forward and backward) are reversed compared to Internet explorer This is useful to put the 'go to next image' functionality to the button that is better reachable e.g. Hitting Backwards button goes Forward in Lucid Viewer	
Default Selection Mode	
By default, Left-click and drag enables selection mode whenever pan is not available. CTRL+Left-click and drag enables selection mode when zoomed in. Set this to false to only use selection mode when CTRL is pressed	
Mouse Wheel Zoom Speed	
Zoom speed with mouse wheel, 1.0 means default speed, smaller values slower zoom, larger faster zoom	
Reload When Displayed Image Changed	
If true, reloads the currently displayed image automatically when it is changed by an external program on disk. Also reloads the image list when a file in the current directory is added or deleted. Set to false to turn off this behavior.	
High Quality Resampling	
Set to true to use high quality sampling as default.	
Down Sampling Filter	
DownSamplingFilter can be BestQuality, NoAliasing or Narrow The BestQuality filter produces a very small amount of aliasing. The NoAliasing filter is a Lanczos filter that has almost no aliasing when sharpen is set to zero The Narrow filter produces quite a lot of aliasing but will sharpen much and also sharpens 100% images	
Auto Rotate EXIF	
If true, JPEG images are auto rotated according to EXIF image orientation tag if present.	
Minimal Display Time	
Minimal display time of an image when manually navigating (with keyboard or mouse) (in milliseconds [0..1000 ms])	
Force GDI Plus	
Force using GDI+ for reading JPEG. Only use when you have problems reading your JPEGs with the default Turbo JPEG library. Note that using GDI+ is slower than the Turbo JPEG library! (Setting to true automatically disables Animated PNG support)	
Use Embedded Color Profiles	
If true, embedded ICC color profiles are used for JPEG, PNG and TIFF. This forces using GDI+ and therefore results in much slower loading of images! Only set to true if you really need this. (ICC color profiles are not supported for Animated PNG)	
Transparency Color	
Color used for transparent parts of images, R G B format as used by BackgroundColor	
Auto Zoom Mode	
Auto zoom mode (for window mode only if AutoZoomModeFullscreen is present) FitNoZoom : Fit images to screen, never enlarge image FillNoZoom : Fill screen with no black borders, crop if necessary but not too much, never enlarge image Fit : Fit images to screen Fill : Fill screen with no black borders, crop if necessary	
Auto Zoom Mode Fullscreen	
Auto zoom mode for fullscreen mode. If empty, same value as 'AutoZoomMode' is used.	
Zoom Pause Percent	
For convenience, when zooming continuously, it will pause at the set percent (default 100%) briefly before continuing in either direction This ensures that you can always zoom in or zoom out to the set percent reliably regardless of image size or zoom steps default: 100 set to 0 to disable the pause	
Contrast correction to apply to all images. Must be in -0.5 .. 0.5 Values > 0 increase contrast, values < 0 decrease contrast	
Gamma	
Gamma correction to apply to all images. Must be between 0.5 and 2 Use gamma<1 to increase brightness and gamma>1 to decrease brightness	
Color saturation to apply to all images. Must be in 0.0 .. 2.0 0.0 means gray scale image, 1.0 no additional color saturation, 2.0 maximal saturation	
Sharpening to apply for downsampled images. Must be in 0 .. 0.5 Note that for 100 % zoom, the BestQuality filter will not apply any sharpening, only the other filters do	
Unsharp Mask Parameters	
Default parameters for unsharp masking: Radius Amount Threshold Note: unsharp masking cannot be applied automatically to every image This setting only provides the default parameters when entering the unsharp mask mode	
RT Show Grid Lines	
Default parameters for controlling rotation and perspective correction	
RT Auto Crop	
RT Preserve Aspect Ratio	
Cyan Red	
Default color balance. Negative values for C,M,Y correction, positive for R,G,B. Values must be in -1.0 .. +1.0	
Magenta Green	
Yellow Blue	
Default Fixed Crop Size	
The initial crop window size when using 'Fixed Size' crop mode	
User Crop Aspect Ratio	
User defined crop aspect ratio (x y), meaning (x : y) Shows up as last item in crop popup menu	
Show EXIF Date In Title	
Show the acquisition date from EXIF data in the window title	
Show File Path In Title	
Show full file path and name in the window title (shows only file name by default)	
Show File Name	
Set to true to initially display the file name of each image in the upper, left corner of the screen	
File Name Format	
The elements to show when showing the file name. Possible elements: %filename% : File name %filepath% : File name and path %index% : Index of image in folder, e.g. [1/12] %zoom% : Current zoom factor %size% : Size of image in pixels (w x h) %filesize% : Size of image on disk	
File Name Font	
Font for the file name display, see DefaultGUIFont key for the format	
Show File Info	
Set to true to initially display the file info box (EXIF info if available)	
Show JPEG Comments	
Set to true to show JPEG comments (EXIF user comment, EXIF image description or JPEG comment) in the file info box	
Show Histogram	
Set to true to show the histogram on the file info panel by default	
GPS Map Provider	
URL for the map provider to display GPS coordinates on a map (only shown when EXIF has GPS coordinates) OpenStreetmap: www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat={lat}&mlon={lng}&zoom=15 Google maps: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query={lat},{lng}	
Metadata Fields	
Fields of the Metadata tab that differ from the default, separated by semicolons. Normally only the common fields are shown. +name shows a field, -name hides it and +* shows all fields. The names are those of the Windows property system, e.g. +System.Photo.MakerNote;-System.Comment. The easiest way to change it is 'Choose fields...' on the Metadata tab.	
Auto Contrast Correction	
Automatic contrast correction by histogram equalization F5 enables/disables the correction on the current image.	
ACC Exclude	
Using the following two keys, it is possible to explicitly exclude/include folders from the contrast correction. More specific patterns have precedence over less specific patterns and inclusion has precedence over exclusion if a folder matches both. Example: '*\pics\orig\* has precedence over *\pics\* because it is more specific Use the ; character to separate two expressions. Example: ACCExclude=%mypictures%\Digicam\edited\*;*.bmp This will exclude all files in the ..\My Pictures\Digicam\edited\ folder and all its subfolders and all bmp files from automatic contrast correction. The following two placeholders are recognized: %mypictures% : "My documents\My Pictures" folder %mydocuments% : "My documents" folder	
ACC Include	
Auto Contrast Correction Amount	
Amount of automatic contrast correction 0 means no contrast correction, 1 means full (to black and white point) contrast correction. Must be in (0 .. 1)	
Amount of color correction in the color channels reg, green, blue, cyan, magenta and yellow The numbers must be between 0.0 (no correction) and 1.0 (total correction towards the gray world model) Set all values to 0 to disable color correction	
Auto Brightness Correction Amount	
Amount of automatic brightness correction 0 means no brightness correction, 1 means full correction to middle gray. Must be in (0 .. 1)	
Local Density Correction	
Automatic correction of local density (local brightness of images) Can be enabled/disabled on the image with F6	
LDC Exclude	
See remark about exclusion/inclusion at the ACCExclude setting. The same applies to these settings.	
LDC Include	
LDC Brighten Shadows	
Amount of local density correction of shadows Can be in [0, 1]	
LDC Brighten Shadows Steepness	
Deep shadow steepness of enhancement Can be in [0, 1], values bigger than 0.9 are not recommended	
LDC Darken Highlights	
Amount of local density correction of highlights Can be in [0, 1]	
Landscape Mode	
Set to true to turn on landscape enhancement mode automatically	
Landscape Mode Params	
Parameter set used in landscape enhancement mode Space separated, use -1 to leave parameter untouched Contrast Gamma Sharpen ColorCorrection ContrastCorrection LightenShadows DarkenHighlights DeepShadows CyanRed MagentaGreen YellowBlue Saturation	
Max Slide Show File List Size KB	
Maximum size of slide show text files in KB	
Slide Show Transition Effect	
Transition effect for slide shows in full screen mode - ignored when used in window mode Possible transition effects: None, Blend, SlideRL, SlideLR, SlideTB, SlideBT, RollRL, RollLR, RollTB, RollBT, ScrollRL, ScrollLR, ScrollTB, ScrollBT	
Slide Show Effect Time	
Time of the slide show transition effect in milliseconds, only used in full screen mode	
Overwrite Original File Without Save Dialog	
If set to true, Ctrl-S overwrites the original file on disk, applying the current processings without showing a dialog or prompting the user to confirm. CAUTION: Use at your own risk! Be aware that the original image file is overwritten and cannot be restored!	
Crop Without Prompt Lossless JPEG	
If set to true, lossless JPEG transformations will crop the image as needed without prompting the user. This will remove 15 pixel rows/columns at the image borders in worst case. CAUTION: Use at your own risk! Be aware that the original image file is overwritten and the cropped borders cannot be restored!	
Delete Confirmation	
Type of confirmation required when deleting a file with the 'x' button on the navigation panel Possible values: Never, OnlyWhenNoRecycleBin, Always OnlyWhenNoRecycleBin means to only require a confirmation when there is no recycle bin available (e.g. on memory sticks) Notice: Does not apply to deleting files with the Del key. To change this edit the KeyMap.txt and assign another command to the Del key.	
Default Save Format	
Default format for saving files. Supported formats: jpg, bmp, png, tif, webp	
JPEG Save Quality	
Quality when saving JPEG files (in 0..100 where 100 is the highest quality)	
WEBP Save Quality	
Quality when saving WEBP files with lossy compression (in 0..100 where 100 is the highest quality)	
Create Param DB Entry On Save	
Set to true to create a parameter DB entry when saving an image with Lucid Viewer to avoid processing it again	
Print Margin	
Default print margin (all sides) in centimeters	
Print Width	
Default print width in centimeters. Use negative numbers to set the 'Fit to paper' printing mode.	
Units	
Units (centimeters, inches) used, one of 'auto', 'metric' or 'english'. 'auto' uses the system setting 'metric' uses the metric system, e.g. centimeters for length 'english' uses the English/US system, e.g. inches for length	
uses the system setting	
uses the metric system, e.g. centimeters for length	
uses the English/US system, e.g. inches for length	
User Cmd 0	
Save the changes to %s?	
The image was cropped, resized or drawn on. Without saving, the changes are lost.	
Don't save	
Save the changed settings?	
Save the changed keyboard shortcuts?	
Drag over the text to copy it, double click copies a line, Ctrl+A selects all, Esc ends.	
%d words were copied to the clipboard.	
Marks the text in the image, drag over it to copy it
